question:
Why is the viewport meta tag critical for media queries?
```html
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
```
options: Sets viewport width to device width for proper breakpoints
explanation: Without this meta tag, mobile browsers default to a wide viewport (often 980px), making min-width breakpoints match incorrectly.

options: When OS or browser prefers dark mode
explanation: prefers-color-scheme respects the operating system's dark/light preference; users set this in OS settings or browser.
Comma (,) is the OR operator in media queries; each comma-separated condition is evaluated separately.
width is the actual viewport width (affected by zoom); device-width is the physical screen size (ignored zoom).
The width property without min/max is an exact match; only viewports precisely 768px wide match.
@supports checks browser CSS feature support; media queries check device/viewport characteristics; use both for robust layouts.
Breakpoints should align with design intent, not device names; common patterns are 640px (tablet), 1024px (desktop), but always test and adjust.
